 Looking to add to your watchlist? Bhuvan Bam navigates a chaotic romantic comedy arc in Dhindora season 2, and Matt Damon embarks on a gruelling ten-year voyage home in Christopher Nolan's epic adaptation of The Odyssey By Prabal Sharma 16 November 2026 Bhuvan Bam in season 2 of Dhindora It's time for your weekly update on the latest OTT releases, and the next seven days have the perfect blend of movies and TV shows to satiate all your binge-watching needs. Bhuvan Bam returns for the second season of Dhindora , stepping into ten distinct roles to drive a chaotic romantic comedy arc; six friends reunite at Excel University to face a major campus scandal in the second season of Campus Diaries ; Nicolas Cage portrays legendary football icon John Madden in the biographical sports drama MADDEN ; Christopher Nolan's adaptation of Homer's The Odyssey becomes available on demand with Matt Damon as Odysseus; Julia Garner and Anthony Boyle star in Graham Moore's biographical limited series chronicling the cryptocurrency collapse in The Altruists .
 Campus Diaries Season 2 (November 18) 
 The second season of this Hindi college drama follows six friends returning to Excel University. Harsh Beniwal, Ritvik Sahore, Abhinav Sharma, Srishti Ganguly Rindani, Saloni Gaur, and Salonie Patel all reprise their respective starring roles. The new episodes track the group as they navigate the escalating complexities of young adulthood. When a severe scandal unexpectedly erupts on campus, the students are forced to set aside their personal conflicts and unite to demand justice.
 Streaming on Prime Video 
 Gordon (November 18) 
 Rodrigo de la Serna stars as the real-life figure Aníbal Gordon in this Argentine biographical crime series. Adapted from Marcelo Larraquy's book, the narrative tracks Gordon's evolution through the 1970s, chronicling his transition from a small-time art thief to a convicted murderer and operative for the Argentine Anticommunist Alliance. Matías Recalt, Camila Peralta, and Matías Mayer complete the leading cast in this six-episode historical thriller detailing his extensive criminal activities.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 Guarding Stars (November 18) 
 Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum directs this holiday romantic comedy adapted from Katherine Center's novel, The Bodyguard . Leighton Meester stars as Hannah Brooks, a practical security professional assigned to protect famous action star Jack Stapleton, played by Jared Padalecki, from a persistent stalker. When the protective detail relocates to a Montana ranch for Christmas, the pair must pose as a couple to keep his family from worrying, severely complicating their professional boundaries. The supporting cast features Andie MacDowell, CM Punk, Noah LaLonde and Walker
Hayes.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 MADDEN (November 18) 
 This biographical sports drama chronicles the multifaceted career of American football icon John Madden. Nicolas Cage stars in the titular role, tracing his journey from coaching the Oakland Raiders to a Super Bowl victory alongside team owner Al Davis, played by Christian Bale. The narrative subsequently follows Madden's transition into a legendary broadcasting career and his pivotal partnership with Electronic Arts founder Trip Hawkins, portrayed by John Mulaney, to develop the massively successful Madden NFL video game franchise. The supporting cast features Kathryn Hahn as Virginia Madden and Sienna Miller as Carol Davis.
 Streaming on Prime Video 
 Mr & Mrs Office (November 18) 
 A Tamil romantic comedy series, Mr & Mrs Office follows a newlywed couple, Arivu and Aishwarya, played by Pradeep Antony and Smeha Manimegalai. Despite their domestic life together, the pair must pretend to be strangers at their shared workplace. The narrative tracks their attempts to navigate complex corporate dynamics under a demanding boss while struggling to keep their marriage a secret from their colleagues.
 Streaming on JioHotstar 
 The Law of Beasts (November 18) 
 Director and co-writer Kasper Bajon helms this four-episode Polish drama spanning two distinct timelines. In 1988, a child murder investigation permanently fractures the friendship between police major Anna Bersz and psychiatrist Agnieszka Grabska, as they disagree on how to handle suspect Mariusz Trynkiewicz. Twenty-five years later, the convicted killer reaches the end of his sentence and is slated for release. The two women, now a government official and a leading psychiatric expert, are forced to reunite and navigate the complex legal challenges of protecting society from a dangerous individual without violating the established rule of law.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 The Odyssey (November 18) 
 Christopher Nolan writes and directs this epic action adaptation of Homer's ancient Greek poem. Shot entirely on IMAX 70mm film cameras, the narrative follows Odysseus, played by Matt Damon, as he endures a gruelling ten-year voyage home following the brutal fall of Troy. While he battles mythical threats across treacherous seas, his wife Penelope, portrayed by Anne Hathaway, is forced to fend off dozens of aggressive suitors led by Robert Pattinson's Antinous. Tom Holland co-stars as their son Telemachus, who launches his own desperate search to find his missing father. The massive ensemble cast features Zendaya as Athena and Lupita Nyong'o in a dual role as Helen of Troy and Clytemnestra.
 Available to buy & rent on Apple TV, BookMyShow Stream, Prime Video 
 Valentina and the 12 Signs (November 18) 
 This eight-episode Brazilian romantic comedy series is adapted from Ray Tavares' novel. Giovanna Grigio stars as the titular character, a young woman who blames her recent devastating breakup entirely on astrological incompatibility. Seeking methodical revenge, she embarks on a mission to date one man from each of the twelve zodiac signs and document every encounter on a live broadcast. Her carefully structured plan quickly unravels when she unexpectedly falls for a suitor who possesses no astrological sign at all.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 Win The Mall (November 18) 
 Hosted by digital creator and model Haley Baylee, this unscripted reality competition series from Fremantle relocates ten teams of two into a fully operational shopping centre. Filmed inside the CF Sherway Gardens mall in Toronto, the eight-episode production challenges the contestants to live inside the retail complex while competing in various physical and fashion-oriented tasks to claim storefronts. The duos must forge strategic alliances and outsmart their rivals to secure a one-million-dollar cash prize. The series also features guest appearances by television personality Jonathan Van Ness, food critic Keith Lee, and content creators Salish Matter and Lilly Singh.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 The Altruists (November 19) 
 Creator Graham Moore and co-showrunner Jacqueline Hoyt helm this eight-episode biographical limited series chronicling the meteoric rise and devastating collapse of cryptocurrency exchange FTX. Julia Garner and Anthony Boyle star as Caroline Ellison and Sam Bankman-Fried, two ambitious prodigies who initially set out to revolutionise the global financial system. The narrative tracks their deeply toxic romantic relationship and escalating series of catastrophic decisions as they ultimately face accusations of stealing eight billion dollars from their customers. The ensemble cast features Karan Soni, Paul Reiser, Robin Weigert, Jennifer Grey and Terry Chen.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 Dhindora Season 2 (November 20) 
 Creator and star Bhuvan Bam returns for the second season of his comedy series, which transitions entirely to Netflix for its new episodes. The show shifts its focus to a romantic comedy arc centred on the character Titu Mama. The narrative explores the chaotic aftermath when Titu's past unexpectedly collides with his wife's strict village traditions, dragging the rest of the family into a series of complicated romantic mishaps. Bam reprises his numerous distinct roles to play ten different characters throughout the season.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 Perfect Liars (November 20) 
 An adaptation of Álex Mírez's novel, this Spanish young adult thriller is set within an elite university. Irene Balmes stars as Jude Derry, a determined student who deliberately challenges the three wealthy Cash brothers dominating the Tagus campus. As she attempts to unravel the dark secrets surrounding Aegan, Adrik, and Aleixandre, her investigation threatens to completely dismantle their powerful family empire while exposing dangerous truths from her own past.
 Streaming on Prime Video 
 Primetime Preacher$ (November 20) 
 Academy Award-nominated director Joe Berlinger helms this documentary examining the massive 1980s religious media empires built by televangelists Jim Bakker, Jerry Falwell and Jimmy Swaggart. The film chronicles how the three figures transformed traditional Sunday morning preaching into highly lucrative broadcasting networks. As extreme wealth and ambition collide, the narrative tracks the explosive public sex scandals and bitter rivalries that eventually ignited a devastating holy war between the prominent leaders.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 Steps (November 20) 
 A comedic reimagining of the classic Cinderella fairy tale. Ali Wong voices Lilith, a misunderstood and rebellious stepsister who accidentally transforms her sibling Margot, played by Stephanie Hsu, into a frog. When this magical mishap allows a mean-spirited girl named Priscilla to seize control of the kingdom, Lilith must form an unlikely alliance with Cinderella, voiced by Amanda Seyfried. The group teams up with a troll to save their home and reverse the spell. The extensive voice cast also features Nikki Glaser as the villainous Priscilla alongside Daniel Radcliffe, Young Mazino, Peter Dinklage and Bette Midler.
 Streaming on Netflix 
 The Blue Road (November 20) 
 This cross-border crime thriller series is a co-production between South Korea and Japan. Adapted from a 2002 manhwa, the narrative follows a joint investigation triggered by a string of bizarre international murders. When a victim is discovered in Tokyo with Korean letters written in blood and another surfaces in South Korea accompanied by Japanese text, two detectives must bridge their jurisdictional divides. Son Suk-ku stars as the Korean investigator, paired with Eita Nagayama as his Japanese counterpart to track down the serial killer.
 Streaming on Netflix
